current.text: He is expected to be fine coming into the season.
Experts say it is too early to call him injury prone, and that expecting last season's injuries to repeat would be a mistake. He still has to prove he can stay healthy this year.
Experts think the market has faded him too far after last season's injuries.
Experts value him as a pick 35 to 45 player, in rounds 3 to 4. They are happy to draft him around pick 45.
Pick 24 is too early for him. A 29 USD price in an auction mock was called too high.
More minutes plus better shooting and defensive stats should make him a top-50 player again.
The team may push him to take more threes, even if it costs some efficiency.
OKC lost Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins. That opens up usage. He and Alex Caruso are the only wings left who can guard bigger forwards.
OKC may lean more on offense with SGA, Ajay Mitchell and Williams together. The team is projected to win about 57 to 62 games.

durable.text: Last season he missed the start after wrist surgery, then hurt his hamstring several times after returning. Many of his games came at reduced minutes while he recovered.
Elite defender who can guard positions one through five. Experts call him an All-NBA and All-Defense caliber player.
Takes very few threes, a long-standing concern.
His high block, rebound and FG% rates came when he played center. On a healthy team he plays the three.
Strong in steals, points and assists for a forward. He has no weak category.

note: He cost 35 USD in our last auction. This year Yahoo values him at 26 USD (average cost 22) and ESPN at 20 USD (average cost 18.2). Experts see him as a pick 35 to 45 player and called 29 USD too high, so a bid in the low to mid 20s is fair. He has no weak category, so he fits any build and helps most in steals, assists and points. Early in the season, check that his hamstrings hold up and whether he takes more threes.
